description: String `hello`, empty string, whitespace-only string — Exact string content; empty is distinct from missing and null. — R
String content `null`, `true`, `false`, `42`, `1.25` — Strings stay strings under an explicit string representation/schema. — R
String content `{}`, `{"a":1}`, `[]`, `[1,true]`, `"quoted"` — No JSON inference or double-unquoting of explicit strings. — R
String with spaces, tabs, LF, CRLF, quotes, backslashes — Preserve payload according to the family encoder's escaping rules. DeepSeek/GLM strings are literal; do not impose a global XML decoder. — R
`café`, CJK, combining characters, emoji — Preserve code points; valid Rust `&str` chunk boundaries only. — R
Signed integer 0, -1, 42 — Actual JSON number with exact integer value, not string/bool. — R
Fraction -1.25, exponent `1e2`, integral number `42.0` — Numeric value is correct; require original spelling only on paths promising lexical preservation. — R
`9007199254740993`, i64 min/max, just above i64 max, u64 max — No f64 rounding, saturating cast, or replacement with null. Inspect emitted numeric lexeme when `Value` cannot preserve it. — T
Very large valid JSON integer beyond u64 — Exact raw number on paths that support it; otherwise explicit documented fallback/error. Never assert through f64. — C
`true` and `false` — Boolean types, never numeric 1/0 or strings. — R
Bare null versus encoded string `null` — Distinct values when wire syntax can represent both. Schema-directed ambiguity follows B01–B04. — R
Empty and nested object, empty and heterogeneous array — Preserve shape, member types, and element order. — R
Malformed numeric `1x`, `NaN`, `Infinity`, `1e9999` — Family's explicit fallback/error; never malformed JSON, saturation, silent zero, or fabricated success. — T

Numeric/boolean compatibility spellings `+1`, `01`, `TRUE`, `1`, `yes`, `None` — Separate legacy acceptance rules from standard JSON. Pin known behavior per family; do not infer a universal coercion. — C
Omitted optional property versus explicit null versus empty string — Three distinct outputs; no synthesized keys/defaults. — R
JSON object containing string `"42"` and numeric `42` — Decode once; do not recursively coerce already typed JSON merely because a child schema differs. — R
`{type:string}`, raw `null` — String `null`. — R
`{type:[string,null]}`, raw `null` — JSON null under the proposed GLM/Qwen/M3 nullable preference. — R
`anyOf` / `oneOf` of string and null, both branch orders — Same nullable preference; explicit wire string still stays string. — R
`{type:string,nullable:true}`, raw `null` — Qwen compatibility extension permits null; other families require an explicit supported/unsupported result. — C
Nullable integer / number / boolean via type array, anyOf, oneOf — Test both null and non-null member: 42, 1.25, false. Exact type. — R
String-or-integer with raw `42` — GLM's declared verbatim-string preference; independently pin Qwen/MiniMax policy. Schema validity alone cannot resolve ambiguity. — C
`{anyOf:[{type:integer,minimum:100},{enum:["30"]}]}`, raw `30` — String `30`, the valid string candidate; catches #280 and current v2 gap. — R
B07 with `const:"30"` — Same; const must contribute type information. — R
Integer alternative plus unconstrained `{}`, raw `30` — GLM preserves its string fallback; absence of a string hint is not proof strings are excluded. — R
`anyOf:[{const:"auto"},{type:integer}]`, raw `auto` / `42` — String `auto` / number 42; string-literal alternative does not allow every string. — R
`allOf:[{type:[string,integer]},{type:integer}]`, raw `7` — Number 7; constraints intersect. — R
Top-level `type:string` plus `anyOf:[string,null]`, raw `null` — String `null`; siblings narrow the union. — R
`type:[string,null]` plus `oneOf:[string,integer]`, raw `null` — String `null`; the sibling excludes JSON null. — R
`allOf:[{type:number},{type:integer}]`, raw `7` — Number 7; integer is included in number. — R
`allOf` with annotation-only sibling and nested composition — An annotation is unconstrained, not false; nested type intersections remain effective. — R
Enum/const without `type`, including `42.0`, null, string `null` — Infer only supported literal types; integral numeric literals remain numeric. — R
String/null schema with enum permitting only string `null` — Do not select JSON null simply because the type list permits it. — T
Reorder union branches; wrap in `allOf:[schema,{}]`; add title/description — Unambiguous result is invariant. Ambiguous selection must not accidentally depend on first branch. — T
Contradictory types, false schema, impossible enum — Bounded conservative behavior; parser does not claim schema validation. Strict grammar rejects every invalid candidate. — C

Overlapping oneOf branches, e.g. integer and number — Type inference is not exclusive-branch validation. Grammar/validator must reject a candidate matching both; parser must not falsely report schema compliance. — C
Local `$ref` to string; JSON-looking raw body — Preserve string exactly. — R
Local `$ref` to object; raw object JSON — Object, not double-encoded string. — R
Reference to nullable scalar / array / object — Same supported result as equivalent inline schema. — T
Two-hop reference chain — Same result as direct target. — R
Pointer segments with `~0`, `~1`; Unicode names — Resolve the exact key, no accidental path splitting. — R
Percent-encoded URI fragment: object reference resolves to the correct target. Target for schema-directed parsers; explicit grammar reference cases are in G08.
References into `#/properties/...`, legacy `definitions`, and root `#` — Correct original root; no rebasing to the extracted property. Recursive root separately bounded. — T
$ref plus sibling type narrowing string/integer to integer: explicit sibling integer yields 42 on all schema-directed families.
Missing target and malformed pointer — No panic, partial mutation, external fetch, or traversal escape; family fallback is deterministic. — R
Self-cycle, two-node cycle, branching cycle — Bounded traversal work, not just depth; no stack overflow or exponential search. Use deterministic counters where available. — R

Acyclic chains of depth 4 and 64, plus unrelated numeric argument alongside a cyclic reference: bounded fallback without losing unrelated arguments. Internal budget-counter assertions remain in the existing parser unit suites.
`$ref`-looking objects inside enum, const, default, examples — Preserve literal data; never treat it as a schema node. — R
`$id`, nested resource scope, external `$ref`, anchors — Either supported with correct scope or explicit conservative fallback; never resolve against the wrong document. — R/C
Two tools reuse identical `$defs` names with different target types — Resolve in the selected tool's root; no cross-tool cache contamination. — T
Root `parameters` itself is referenced — Required/properties survive extraction where supported; missing support is explicit. — T
MiniMax M3 nested `{page:2,per_page:10}` under object/null union — Both children numeric, under anyOf and type-array forms. — R
M3 union containing string, array, and exactly one object branch — Object branch's child schemas selected for nested tags. — R
Two object alternatives with conflicting child types — Preserve documented ambiguous fallback; never arbitrarily choose the first object branch. — R
Object plus unconstrained alternative — Unconstrained alternative counts as potentially object; no false uniqueness. — R
Nested arrays of typed scalars and objects; nullable `items` — Correct child schema at each depth, no stringification of numeric grandchildren. — T
Schema-valued additionalProperties — Undeclared nested key uses that schema where supported; false/absent variants are distinct. — T
Zero-argument call — Exactly one call with `{}`; not absent arguments, null, or empty string. — R
Arguments emitted `z,a,m` — Source order on paths whose output promises it; validate raw JSON separately from semantic equality. — R
Duplicate z after a: last value wins at the first key position on XML/XTML paths; no concatenation of repeated values.
Two tools share parameter `x`, one string, one number, called in both orders — Each call uses its own schema; stable distinct call indices. — T
Separate requests redefine the same tool name/schema — Fresh parser or supported reinitialization cannot retain prior request's schema/state. — T

Unknown tool, unknown argument, absent tools, empty tools, absent parameters, `{}`/true/false schema — Explicit per-family fallback/acceptance, no panic and no silently substituted shared default tool. — C
Input schema before and after parse, including failed parse — Identical JSON tree; parser/grammar normalization must not mutate caller-owned schema. — T
Kimi K2 — JSON argument object with all scalar types, nested containers, escaped strings, call IDs containing indices; decode exactly once. Marker text inside JSON strings remains data.

Kimi K3 — `type=string` with `null`, JSON, spaces, marker-looking text; typed number/boolean/null/object/array; missing type defaults to string; malformed typed value follows explicit raw-string fallback. Do not confuse current parser syntax checking with validating that the tag's type matches every JSON body.
DeepSeek V3 / V3.1 — Native fenced/JSON envelopes, same argument corpus; strings that resemble scalars stay quoted strings. Exercise each registry entry independently.
DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 — `string=true` preserves `  café\n`, whitespace-only, empty, and `null`; `string=false` decodes valid JSON. A conflicting tool schema cannot override the wire flag.

DeepSeek V4.1 — Spaced XML parameters and JSON-object invocation bodies; nested marker-like strings, escaped quotes, Unicode; mixed dialect calls through the V4 adapter. A raw JSON array at the invocation root is not an object call.
GLM — Literal `<`, `&`, `"`, numeric entity spellings, and `{"text":"""}` inside an object; no global entity decoding. Existing #249 coverage is v2-specific: include v1.
MiniMax M2 — Shared XML coercion cases including string `null`, unions, argument order, duplicate replacement; M3 fixes do not automatically cover M2. Pin its actual entity-encoding contract.
MiniMax M3 — Namespace-prefixed nested tags, nullable pagination, referenced objects, text/array/object node selection and schema ownership. Include `_nom` alias smoke.

Qwen2.5 versus Qwen3-Coder — JSON and XML are separate dialects. Qwen XML streaming: non-nullable string can stream eagerly; nullable or otherwise ambiguous value must not commit a string prefix before selecting null/number.
Muse JSON-first decoding and exact raw fallback; schema cannot redefine explicit JSON types. Ordered to=self / tool / to=user events are covered by F07.

Gemma — `<|"|>` string delimiters around `42`/`null`; unquoted numeric/bool/null values; nested arrays and objects; literal `call:` and `<tool_call|>` inside strings; malformed delimiters never manufacture a completed call.

GPT-OSS — Harmony directed tool messages with JSON arguments; text and actual token-ID input, including non-ASCII token splits; `analysis`/`final` must not become tools. Preserve quoted versus unquoted types; no native Unified claim.
Whole input, every valid two-part split, character chunks, and seeded multipart chunks produce the authored result. Include empty chunks. Compare each to the oracle, not merely to each other.
Split inside `null`, negative/exponent numbers, escaped quotes, backslashes, Unicode, and closing markers. No type change or invalid accumulated JSON.

For each emitted call, concatenate raw argument deltas by index and parse them independently of `assemble`; name emitted once, stable index, one completion transition, no argument updates after completion.

Inspect Qwen's output before parameter/function close: permitted string streaming begins early; ambiguous nullable/union values cannot emit a prefix that must later be retracted. Assert valid final JSON in both cases.

Truncate before value, mid-scalar, mid-string escape, before parameter close, after parameter close, after invoke close, and before outer close. Only a family's explicitly documented complete-inner-call recovery may complete. No fabricated `{}` or valid-prefix-only arguments.
One complete call followed by a truncated call: first retained exactly once; second cannot become a completed call. Check raw deltas as well as coalesced calls.

Reasoning → call → reasoning → text, with a schema-sensitive argument: Exact ordered Unified events, untouched argument body. Legacy tool projection preserves markers where its contract requires them (#253); do not require legacy aggregate ordering it cannot represent.

`None`, reasoning-prefilled, and response-prefilled initialization: Correct channel and same argument types for equivalent logical call. Run on each native Unified family; do not select init by sniffing input.

Guided JSON named and required tool output: Typed JSON preserved; named arguments get the selected tool; required arrays keep call order. Test Reject, RecoverAsText, StreamBestEffort semantics once at their shared owner plus one routing case per family.

Guided valid first call + invalid later call: Reject emits no committed call; RecoverAsText recovers atomically; StreamBestEffort follows its per-call promise. Null/array/string root arguments do not become an empty object call.

Finish with pending prefix; reset/reinitialize where supported: No old bytes, call indices, or channel state leak into next turn. Test repeated `finish()` only if the API promises it is legal; otherwise pin the documented error.
Two calls in one chunk, two in adjacent chunks, repeated tool name: No merging of distinct calls, duplicate dispatch, or schema borrowed from the preceding call.
Generate nullable string alternatives via type list and anyOf — String/null accepted; wrong numeric type and unknown argument key rejected.
Generate numeric union with `enum:[1,null]` / const — 1/null accepted; 42 rejected. Type narrowing must not discard value constraints.
Direct and referenced string enum/const — Allowed literal accepted, other literal rejected, both direct and in string/null union.
Min/max string length and pattern — Boundary accepted/rejected strings, including empty string when schema allows it; UTF-8 character semantics as supported by pinned grammar engine.
Escaped regex dollar/anchor/backslash parity — `^price\$` compiles and accepts `price$`; stripping anchors must not leave an invalid regex.

Integer/number bounds, enum, multipleOf; nested object/array constraints — Valid candidates accepted and targeted invalid candidates rejected on the strict supported path. No overclaim from a structural-tag JSON snapshot.

Required and optional fields, zero-field object, additionalProperties:false — Required omission and unknown fields rejected on a path claiming strict support; optional omission/empty object accepted when valid. #274 documents an existing required-omission limitation—keep that separate from its nullable fix.
Referenced object and deep reference to marker enum — Correct XTML type and payload accepted; quoted object, wrong tag type, wrong marker value rejected.
Recursive object reference and extracted local root — Valid finite recursive object accepted and schema compiles; do not drop an optional property merely because it is recursive.
Const/enum/default/examples containing literal `{"$ref":"literal"}` — Literal data preserved; no traversal as a schema reference.

Strict absent / true / false × Auto / forced strict — Shared builder policy matches the chosen implementation revision. #196 changes omitted strict to declared-schema enforcement; main and candidate expectations must be labeled separately.
Named / required / auto, parallel calls false/true — Correct declared name, no duplicate required keys, cardinality follows request; auto still permits plain response.
Unsupported composition/reference scope/work budget — Explicit existing fallback stays parser-compatible; report loss of strict enforcement, never call fallback a schema-validating path.
Accepted Kimi grammar payloads for each JSON type: real XGrammar complete-language acceptance, followed by exact arguments on v1 batch, v1 jail, v2 tool, and native Unified.

Same input with per-case tools: real Unified YAML emitter preserves distinct string and nullable schemas. Direct type behavior is covered by B01/B02; downstream stages are blocked if emission loses tools.
Schema override absent versus explicit empty tools list — Only absence uses default inventory; explicit `[]` stays empty.
YAML generator → Rust loader → live parser — Preserve full tool definitions, `$defs`, refs, required, strict false, and null values. One real cross-language test owns this composition risk.
Capture schema differs from recorded request schema — Validation fails; no fallback to a generic/shared schema.
Family/case missing from runner or implementation unavailable — Missing expected coverage fails the inventory gate; unavailable surface reported explicitly and separately from pass count.
New expected behavior versus historical capture — Current code must run against authored expectations; historical output is immutable evidence, not an automatically rewritten oracle.
Huge integers and argument key order — Assertion path retains numeric lexemes and source order where required; do not reduce everything to a lossy float/map comparison.
Invalid/incomplete raw call deltas filtered by `assemble` — Raw stream assertion still fails even if the final assembled event list looks clean.
